tasks.title: Lock fix: CK5 markProjectComplete can complete a cancelled order and release installer retention
tasks.phase: P1 · Foundation: true names, clean schema, dead code out
tasks.notes: CkInspectionTransitions.php:139 — add status re-check with lockForUpdate() inside a DB::transaction.

prep.what: Prevent the CK5 workflow step from completing an already-cancelled project and erroneously releasing installer retention pay.
prep.understand: Race: a project is cancelled (status flips) while a concurrent call to markProjectComplete reads the pre-cancel status. Without a lock, both reads see non-cancelled and proceed. lockForUpdate() forces the second caller to wait and re-read the true post-lock status.
approach: Open CkInspectionTransitions.php:139 — find the markProjectComplete method entry.
Ensure the entire method body is wrapped in `DB::transaction(fn() => ...)`.
Replace the project load with `Project::lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($id)`.
Add early guard: `if ($project->status === 'cancelled') { throw new \LogicException('Cannot complete a cancelled project'); }`
Run CkInspectionTransitions tests.

tasks.title: Lock fix: 3 estimate transitions run with no transaction at all
tasks.phase: P1 · Foundation: true names, clean schema, dead code out

prep.what: Wrap 3 estimate transition methods in DB::transaction() so their multi-record status changes are atomic.
prep.understand: These methods update several related records with no transaction wrapper. A mid-method error leaves the DB in a partial state. Simply wrapping in DB::transaction() is the minimal fix — if any step throws, the whole thing rolls back.
approach: Open EstimateTransitions.php. Go to lines :37, :807, :849 to identify the three transition methods.
For each: wrap the entire method body in `return DB::transaction(function () use (...) { ... });`
Verify no outer transaction already wraps callers (grep for callsites).
Run Estimate-related tests.

tasks.title: Lock fix: workflow root — WorkflowTransitionSupport::transition overwrites phase/substep
tasks.phase: P1 · Foundation: true names, clean schema, dead code out
tasks.notes: WorkflowTransitionSupport.php:135, :270 — use fresh()->lockForUpdate() to prevent concurrent overwrites.

prep.what: Prevent two concurrent workflow transition calls from reading stale phase/substep state and overwriting each other's writes.
prep.understand: transition() reads current phase/substep, computes next, then writes. A second concurrent call reads the same pre-write state and writes conflicting values. This is the root lock defect — fixing it here protects all workflows that use this support class.
approach: Open WorkflowTransitionSupport.php:135 — find where the model is first loaded before transition logic.
Replace the model load with `$model->fresh()->lockForUpdate()` (or add fresh/lockForUpdate if the model isn't refreshed here).
At line :270 — apply the same fresh()->lockForUpdate() pattern to the second read.
Ensure the entire transition block is inside `DB::transaction()`.
Run workflow transition tests.

tasks.title: Lock fix: invoice writes outside a lock
tasks.phase: P1 · Foundation: true names, clean schema, dead code out
tasks.notes: InvoiceStatusRollup.php:10 — 5 write paths need lockForUpdate() on the initial load.

prep.what: Add lockForUpdate() to all 5 write paths in InvoiceStatusRollup so invoice status aggregations are never written on stale reads.
prep.understand: InvoiceStatusRollup reads invoice states and writes a rolled-up status. Two concurrent rollups can both read the same pre-write state and produce conflicting results. lockForUpdate() on the initial load prevents concurrent readers from advancing until the first caller commits.
approach: Open InvoiceStatusRollup.php:10. Grep for `->save()` and `->update()` in this file to identify all 5 write paths.
For each path: trace back to where the relevant record is first loaded. Replace with `->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail()`.
Verify all 5 paths are inside `DB::transaction()`.
Run invoice rollup tests.

tasks.title: Squash 445 migrations into one clean baseline schema; data seeding moves to seeders
tasks.phase: P1 · Foundation: true names, clean schema, dead code out
tasks.notes: artisan schema:dump --prune. Unblocks t58 and t65.

prep.what: Replace 445 individual migration files with a single schema dump so fresh installs are fast and the migration table is clean.
prep.understand: `artisan schema:dump --prune` writes the current DB schema to `database/schema/*.sql` and deletes migration files already reflected in it. Fresh installs run schema.sql then any remaining (post-squash) migrations. This is a destructive-but-reversible git change — commit the schema dump and the deleted migration files in one commit.
approach: Verify all 445 migrations have been run on the local dev DB: `php artisan migrate:status` — all should show 'Ran'.
Run `php artisan schema:dump --prune` — confirm it writes `database/schema/*.sql` and removes migration files.
Spot-check the generated schema.sql: 5-10 known critical tables (projects, estimates, invoices, users, etc.) must be present with correct columns.
Test on a clean DB: `php artisan migrate:fresh` should apply without errors.
Commit the schema dump + deleted migration files together with a clear message.
